A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PrunE research work. All 26 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–L, are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PrunE benchmark results, ablations, edge-identification analyses, and runtime measurements in Section 7 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and additional experiments in Appendix J.3.

M1.justification: The subgraph selector, sampling procedure, graph-size constraint, epsilon-probability alignment, and combined training objective remain unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same GOOD-Motif, GOOD-HIV, OGBG-Molbbbp, DrugOOD EC50, SPMotif, GOOD-CMNIST, and Graph-Twitter coverage. Concept-shift evaluations and SPMotif graphs with two invariant subgraphs already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 1, the GSAT/CIGA/AIA case study, and the appendix comparisons, including LIRS in Tables 5–6.

E3.justification: Sections 7.1 and J.2 retain the same evaluation metrics, data splits, GNN configurations, ERM pretraining, validation-based model selection, and hyperparameter searches. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The regularizer and ERM-pretraining ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity studies, encoder comparisons, and edge-identification analyses and visualizations are unchanged, including those in Appendix J.3.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four runs with different random seeds and report means and standard deviations. Table 1 retains the same p-value threshold of 0.05 for significance markings.

E6.justification: Main-text and appendix result values, rankings, and plotted findings match. For example, Table 1 retains PrunE's GOODMotif-base accuracy of 91.48±0.40, and Table 9 retains its Graph-Twitter accuracy of 63.37±0.76.

T1.justification: Assumption 1, Proposition 1, Theorems 5.1–5.2, and Appendix F's proofs retain the same mathematical content and reasoning. Changes in equation spacing do not alter the definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of a first pruning-based graph OOD method, improved invariant-subgraph preservation, theoretical guarantees, and superior OOD performance.

C2.justification: Both retain the same mechanism explanations, comparisons with LIRS, hyperparameter failure conditions, and applicability boundaries. Appendix K's limitations concerning other modalities and persistent strongly correlated spurious edges are unchanged.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, implementation settings, hyperparameter grids, software versions, GPU information, and code-access statement are unchanged in the main text and Appendices E, J.2, and L.

R1.justification: The references and related-work discussions in Section 6 and Appendix D are unchanged, as is the positioning of pruning against direct invariant-subgraph identification and latent-space disentanglement.

P1.justification: v4 corrects the title's 'Out-of-Distribtuion' spelling and moves Section 3's dataset paragraph before its introductory paragraph. It also introduces the missing space in 'PrunEemploys' in the abstract. These are localized editorial changes.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is reduced in size and moved from the lower-right case-study discussion to the upper-right of page 3 alongside the preliminaries. Its content is unchanged. Nearby text and equations on pages 3–5 are reflowed and respaced.

improvement.justification: v4 corrects a title typo, makes local layout changes around Figure 2, and introduces a missing abstract space. The methods, empirical evidence, proofs, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. These small presentation gains and defects leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
